text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities — A28, A30, A31, A32, A33 and A34 — each ran in only about half of the cases in the earlier window (49–52 in 100); in the later window each of them runs in about 99–100 in 100 cases [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024].
- In the earlier window these six activities formed two mutually exclusive groups: A28/A30/A31 ran together in about 49 in 100 cases and A32/A33/A34 in about 52 in 100, while no case contained activities from both groups (co-occurrence zero); in the later window both groups run together in about 98–100 in 100 cases [REL013, REL015, REL018, REL019, REL022, REL025].
- The cross-group order became fixed: in the later window A25 precedes A28/A30/A31 in about 99 in 100 cases, that group precedes A32/A33/A34 in about 98 in 100, and the second group precedes A26 in about 99 in 100; within each group the order remains unfixed, with each pair appearing in both orders in roughly equal shares [REL001, REL007, REL013, REL015, REL025].
- Successor profiles changed accordingly: in the earlier window A25's outgoing transitions were spread roughly evenly over all six group activities, in the later window they go almost exclusively to A28/A30/A31; A28, A30 and A31 led on to A26 in about 30–36 in 100 of their outgoing transitions before and essentially never do so now, instead leading to A32/A33/A34 [DIR016, DIR018, DIR020, DIR021].
- Distances and positions moved consistently with the second group now always following the first: the gap from A25 to A32/A33/A34 and from A28/A30/A31 to A26 grew from 1–3 event positions to 4–5, A28/A30/A31 occur earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.74 to 0.68), A32/A33/A34 later (about 0.73 to 0.77), A25 earlier (0.67 to 0.62) and A26 later (0.80 to 0.83) [LAG004, LAG007, LAG010, LAG013, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS006].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the exclusive selection between two activity groups was removed, so that both groups now execute in sequence in almost every case. In the earlier window a case ran either the group A28/A30/A31 (about 49 in 100 cases) or the group A32/A33/A34 (about 52 in 100), never both, between the always-present A25 and A26; in the later window both groups run in about 98–100 in 100 cases, first A28/A30/A31 and then A32/A33/A34, with no fixed order inside each group. The change is shown directly and consistently across indicator families: participation of all six activities rose by about 48–50 in 100 cases; cross-group pairs went from never co-occurring to co-occurring in about 98 in 100 cases with the first group always before the second; A28/A30/A31 lost their direct transition to A26, which is now reached from the second group; and distances and trace positions shifted exactly as expected when the second group now always follows the first [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, REL015, REL019, REL022, DIR016, DIR018, DIR020, DIR021, LAG004, LAG007, POS003, POS006]. Limitations: the evidence file contains no screening counts, so the comparison against the number of items expected by chance cannot be made and the judgement rests on the size, directness and consistency of the items (for the core items only about 1 in 200 random re-splits shows a larger difference); and the evidence cannot rule out that the later window contains a different mix of case types in which one branch simply no longer occurs, rather than a routing change within one process.

Other differences:
- A14 and A15 exchanged small shares (A14 about 54 to 49 in 100 cases, A15 about 46 to 52), with A37 routing to A15 correspondingly more often — a small shift in how often two existing alternatives are taken [OCC013, OCC014, DIR026].
- A10 and A11 repeat slightly more often (mean occurrences about 1.55 to 1.66 per trace, recurrence in about 33 to 40 in 100 cases), and A38 somewhat less (about 1.76 to 1.60) [OCC009, OCC010, OCC027].
- Several small routing-share shifts (at A16 towards A25, at A20/A27/A29, and towards A42 from A39/A41) show only moderate empirical strength and may be sampling variation [DIR010, DIR014, DIR017, DIR019, DIR028, DIR029].
